signature: SUBROUTINE ZTGEXC( WANTQ, WANTZ, N, A, LDA, B, LDB, Q, LDQ, Z,

params.name: wantq
params.reference: .TRUE. : update the left transformation matrix Q; .FALSE.: do not update Q.

params.name: wantz
params.reference: .TRUE. : update the right transformation matrix Z; .FALSE.: do not update Z.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the upper triangular matrix A in the pair (A, B). On exit, the updated matrix A.

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, the upper triangular matrix B in the pair (A, B). On exit, the updated matrix B.

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: Q
params.reference: On entry, if `WANTQ` = .TRUE., the unitary matrix Q. On exit, the updated matrix Q. If `WANTQ` = .FALSE., Q is not referenced.

params.name: ldq
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Q. $\mathrm{LDQ} \ge 1$; If `WANTQ` = .TRUE., $\mathrm{LDQ} \ge N$.

params.name: Z
params.reference: On entry, if `WANTZ` = .TRUE., the unitary matrix Z. On exit, the updated matrix Z. If `WANTZ` = .FALSE., Z is not referenced.

params.name: ldz
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Z. $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge 1$; If `WANTZ` = .TRUE., $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge N$.

params.name: ilst
params.reference: Specify the reordering of the diagonal blocks of (A, B). The block with row index `IFST` is moved to row `ILST`, by a sequence of swapping between adjacent blocks.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `=0`: Successful exit.
-   `<0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `=1`: The transformed matrix pair (A, B) would be too far from generalized Schur form; the problem is ill- conditioned. (A, B) may have been partially reordered, and `ILST` points to the first row of the current position of the block being moved.

overrides.reason: The JS API takes IFST and ILST 0-based (base.js and its tests index the diagonal with them directly), unlike ztrexc's 1-based IFST/ILST.
